Differential abundance testing with Milo

Local version, reads from the workshop data repo, no network access

Published

August 4, 2026

Local rework of 3_b_composition_milo.html.

Upstream: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/miloR/inst/doc/milo_gastrulation.html

Method: Dann et al. 2022, “Differential abundance testing on single-cell data using k-nearest neighbor graphs”, Nature Biotechnology, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-021-01033-z

Dataset: Pijuan-Sala et al. 2019, “A single-cell molecular map of mouse gastrulation and early organogenesis”, Nature, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-0933-9

ImportantStatus: transcribed from upstream, first render is a test

The code below is transcribed from the upstream vignette, with the EmbryoAtlasData() download replaced by a read from the staged data repo. It has not been executed yet. error: false is set in the YAML, so any chunk failure stops the render and is reported rather than being buried in the output.

CautionDo not put the download back

Upstream calls EmbryoAtlasData(), which pulls the mouse gastrulation atlas through ExperimentHub. ExperimentHub caches per user, so twenty students on twenty accounts means twenty multi-GB downloads at the same moment. That call is deliberately absent here. It lives in staging/stage_3_b_composition_milo.R and is run once, ahead of time.

Setup

data_dir <- "~/MEGA/workshop_data/3_b_composition_milo"
in_data_dir <- function(basename) {
  return(file.path(data_dir, basename))
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(miloR)
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(scater)
  library(scran)
  library(dplyr)
  library(patchwork)
  library(ggplot2)
})

Load data

Eight samples, four at stage E7.0 and four at E7.5, so the contrast is developmental time. The object already carries a pca.corrected reduction, built after fastMNN batch correction, and cells with an all-NA reduction have already been dropped by the staging script.

NoteStaged file

embryo_atlas_subset.rds, a SingleCellExperiment. Produced by staging/stage_3_b_composition_milo.R, which is where the EmbryoAtlasData() call and the NA filter live.

embryo_data <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "embryo_atlas_subset.rds"))

Visualize the data

embryo_data <- runUMAP(embryo_data, dimred = "pca.corrected", name = "umap")
plotReducedDim(embryo_data, colour_by = "stage", dimred = "umap")

Create a Milo object

Milo extends SingleCellExperiment with slots for the neighbourhoods.

embryo_milo <- Milo(embryo_data)

Construct the KNN graph

k affects the power of the test, because each neighbourhood needs enough cells per sample to estimate between-replicate variance. Too large and it over-smooths. Start with the same k you used for clustering and UMAP.

embryo_milo <- buildGraph(embryo_milo, k = 30, d = 30,
                          reduced.dim = "pca.corrected")

Define representative neighbourhoods

prop is the fraction of cells sampled as neighbourhood indices. refined = TRUE is the recommended sampling scheme.

embryo_milo <- makeNhoods(embryo_milo, prop = 0.1, k = 30, d = 30,
                          refined = TRUE, reduced_dims = "pca.corrected")

Rule of thumb: mean neighbourhood size should be above 5 times the number of samples. If it is lower, raise k or prop and rebuild.

plotNhoodSizeHist(embryo_milo)

Count cells in neighbourhoods

Milo uses the variation in cell numbers between replicates of the same condition to test for differential abundance, so the counting is by sample.

embryo_milo <- countCells(embryo_milo,
                          meta.data = as.data.frame(colData(embryo_milo)),
                          sample = "sample")
head(nhoodCounts(embryo_milo))

Defining the experimental design

Testing is a negative binomial GLM from edgeR. The design matrix maps each sample to its condition, here stage, plus sequencing.batch as a known technical covariate.

TipWorth lingering on

This is the same design-matrix idea as DESeq2 in 2_a_pseudobulk_de_local.qmd, applied to neighbourhood counts instead of gene counts.

embryo_design <- data.frame(colData(embryo_milo))[,
  c("sample", "stage", "sequencing.batch")]

# Batch is stored as an integer, and must be a factor.
embryo_design$sequencing.batch <- as.factor(embryo_design$sequencing.batch)
embryo_design <- dplyr::distinct(embryo_design)
rownames(embryo_design) <- embryo_design$sample

embryo_design
   sample stage sequencing.batch

4       4  E7.5                1
10     10  E7.0                1

Computing neighbourhood connectivity

Milo adapts the spatial FDR correction from cydar, weighting each p-value by the reciprocal of the kth nearest neighbour distance. Those distances have to be stored first.

# This is the slowest step in the workflow.
embryo_milo <- calcNhoodDistance(embryo_milo, d = 30,
                                 reduced.dim = "pca.corrected")

Testing

da_results <- testNhoods(embryo_milo,
                         design = ~ sequencing.batch + stage,
                         design.df = embryo_design,
                         reduced.dim = "pca.corrected")

Inspecting the results

ggplot(da_results, aes(PValue)) + geom_histogram(bins = 50)
ggplot(da_results, aes(logFC, -log10(SpatialFDR))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1)   # 10% FDR

Each node is a neighbourhood, edges show how many cells two neighbourhoods share, and node position comes from the index cell’s position in the single-cell UMAP. Significant neighbourhoods are coloured by log fold change.

embryo_milo <- buildNhoodGraph(embryo_milo)

umap_pl <- plotReducedDim(embryo_milo, dimred = "umap", colour_by = "stage",
                          text_by = "celltype", text_size = 3,
                          point_size = 0.5) +
  guides(fill = "none")

nh_graph_pl <- plotNhoodGraphDA(embryo_milo, da_results, layout = "umap",
                                alpha = 0.1)

umap_pl + nh_graph_pl + plot_layout(guides = "collect")

Differential abundance by cell type

Label each neighbourhood by its most abundant cell type, and record what fraction of the neighbourhood carries that label.

da_results <- annotateNhoods(embryo_milo, da_results, coldata_col = "celltype")
head(da_results)

ggplot(da_results, aes(celltype_fraction)) + geom_histogram(bins = 50)
# Neighbourhoods that are a blend of cell types get called Mixed rather than
# being forced into one label.
da_results$celltype <- ifelse(da_results$celltype_fraction < 0.7,
                              "Mixed", da_results$celltype)
plotDAbeeswarm(da_results, group.by = "celltype")
TipThe teaching payoff

Early types such as epiblast and primitive streak are enriched at the earlier stage, ectoderm later. Note the “Mixed” neighbourhoods that also come up significant. Those are transitional states, and they are exactly what a cluster-level test would have averaged away. That is the argument for Milo over propeller or scCODA in continuum data.

Finding markers of DA populations

findNhoodGroupMarkers runs a one-versus-all differential expression test for a group of neighbourhoods. The grouping has to be defined first, in a NhoodGroup column.

embryo_milo <- logNormCounts(embryo_milo)
# Group the significant neighbourhoods that shifted in one direction against
# everything else. subset.row restricts to 10 genes for illustration, exactly as
# upstream does. Drop that argument for a real analysis.
da_results$NhoodGroup <- as.numeric(da_results$SpatialFDR < 0.1 &
                                    da_results$logFC < 0)
da_nhood_markers <- findNhoodGroupMarkers(
  embryo_milo, da_results,
  subset.row = rownames(embryo_milo)[1:10])
head(da_nhood_markers)
